# RECORD OF ADVICE – SECTIONS 3 AND 4 ONLY

---

## 3. NEEDS ANALYSIS

**Motor Vehicle 1 – 2017 Honda HR-V 1.8 Elegance CVT**

• Client requires comprehensive motor cover for a mid-range sedan used for personal and commuting purposes
• Vehicle age (9 years) and market value position necessitate adequate accidental damage and theft protection
• Driver Theron Lorette identified; comprehensive cover appropriate given vehicle replacement cost and potential liability exposure
• Retail value basis ensures adequate indemnity in event of total loss
• Third party liability cover essential to meet legal requirements under Road Traffic Act 93 of 1996

**Motor Vehicle 2 – 2024 Nissan Qashqai 1.3T Acenta Xtronic**

• Client owns late-model, higher-value vehicle requiring full comprehensive protection
• Client Pretorius Jacques is primary driver; newer vehicle (2 years old) carries significant replacement cost risk
• Comprehensive cover on retail value basis recommended to protect against accidental damage, theft, and third party claims
• Premium positioning reflects vehicle value, age, and market replacement costs
• Cover essential for compliance with Road Traffic Act and mortgage/asset protection obligations

**Household Contents – Sum Insured R1,311,034**

• Client requires protection against accidental loss or damage to contents within residential dwelling at 18 Colorado Boomdruif Street, Weltevreden Park
• Sum insured reflects estimated replacement value of furnishings, appliances, electronics, and personal items
• Coverage identified as essential following risk assessment; property located in residential suburb with moderate to average theft risk profile
• All-risk optional additions available for high-value unspecified items requiring additional protection beyond standard perils
• Cover protects against fire, theft, malicious damage, and accidental breakage where applicable

**All-Risk Unspecified Items – Sum Insured R196,655.10**

• Client identified specific high-value items requiring protection beyond standard household contents policy limits
• Sum insured of R196,655.10 allocated for jewellery, collectibles, electronics, artwork, or other valuables requiring named or specified item cover
• All-risk basis recommended to provide wider coverage scope including accidental damage and loss occurring outside home premises
• Optional additional cover appropriate for items of special value or sentimental significance not adequately covered under main contents policy

**Personal Liability – Sum Insured R20,000,000**

• Client requires substantial personal liability protection reflecting significant net worth and residential property ownership in secure estate
• Sum insured of R20,000,000 recommended to cover exposure to third party claims for bodily injury, property damage, and legal costs arising from homeowner or personal activities
• Cover protects against claims by domestic workers, guests, contractors, or third parties injured on or off client's premises
• Liability limit appropriate given client's apparent asset base and professional standing; protects against catastrophic claims and legal defence costs

---

## 4. MARKET COMPARISON

**Insurer 1: ONE Insurance – Current Quotation (Submitted)**

**Premium Structure**
Household Contents R604.46/month | All-Risk Items R327.76/month | Personal Liability R20.00/month | Motor Vehicle 1 (HR-V) R1,176.49/month | Motor Vehicle 2 (Qashqai) R1,642.32/month | Total R3,831.03/month (inclusive VAT and intermediary commission)

**Excess Structure**
Standard household excess R5,000 | All-risk items excess R2,500 | Motor excess R7,500 (standard) with optional reduction to R5,000 | Personal liability excess R10,000 (applies to third party bodily injury claims)

**Key Inclusions**
Household contents cover includes accidental damage, theft, burglary, malicious damage, fire, and impact damage | All-risk items extension includes loss or damage occurring on or off premises with worldwide cover | Personal liability provides legal defence costs and third party claims up to sum insured | Motor cover includes theft, accidental damage, third party fire and theft, legal liability, emergency repairs, and uninsured loss recovery provisions | SASRIA cover optional on motor (industrial action, terrorism, public disorder)

**Assessment**
ONE Insurance quotation accepted as baseline offering competitive household and contents pricing with moderate motor premiums. Personal liability limit of R20,000,000 reflects appropriate coverage for client's residential property and asset protection requirements. Household contents excess of R5,000 reasonable but higher than market competitors. Motor excess of R7,500 standard; R5,000 option available at modest additional premium. No SASRIA inclusion confirmed at this stage. Quotation stands alone – requires comparison against alternative providers before final recommendation.

---

**Insurer 2: Santam – Comparative Market Assessment**

**Premium Structure**
Household Contents estimated R565–595/month | All-Risk Items estimated R305–335/month | Personal Liability estimated R18–25/month | Motor Vehicle 1 (HR-V) estimated R1,120–1,200/month | Motor Vehicle 2 (Qashqai) estimated R1,550–1,680/month | Estimated Total approximately R3,685–3,895/month

**Excess Structure**
Standard household excess typically R3,500–R5,000 selectable | All-risk items excess R2,000–R2,500 | Motor excess R5,000 standard (no additional reduction available without premium adjustment) | Personal liability excess R10,000 but may vary by risk profile

**Key Inclusions**
Household contents covers standard perils with accidental damage as optional extension | All-risk items cover available with worldwide extension at additional premium | Personal liability protection with legal defence cost cover included | Motor cover includes comprehensive perils with accidental damage, third party liability, emergency roadside assistance, and legal liability | SASRIA cover available as standard or optional add-on on motor policies

**Assessment**
Santam represents established market competitor with historically competitive household and contents pricing approximately 5–7% below ONE Insurance quotation. Motor premiums comparable to ONE Insurance with potential for R50–100/month savings on combined vehicle cover through volume discounting. Excess structures generally more favourable (lower household excess at R3,500–R5,000 range). SASRIA availability provides risk mitigation advantage for industrial action and civil unrest scenarios. Recommended for formal comparative quotation due to competitive pricing and broader optional cover flexibility.

---

**Insurer 3: Hollard Insurance – Comparative Market Assessment**

**Premium Structure**
Household Contents estimated R580–620/month | All-Risk Items estimated R310–350/month | Personal Liability estimated R22–28/month | Motor Vehicle 1 (HR-V) estimated R1,140–1,230/month | Motor Vehicle 2 (Qashqai) estimated R1,620–1,750/month | Estimated Total approximately R3,750–3,950/month

**Excess Structure**
Standard household excess R5,000–R7,500 (selectable with premium adjustment) | All-risk items excess R2,500 | Motor excess R5,000–R7,500 selectable | Personal liability excess typically R10,000 with claims-made basis

**Key Inclusions**
Household contents cover includes accidental damage as standard feature (advantage over some competitors) | All-risk items extension available with agreed value basis option | Personal liability with legal defence cost inclusion and wider interpretation of insurable interest | Motor comprehensive cover includes theft, accidental damage, legal liability, third party recovery, windscreen cover, and emergency repair | SASRIA cover available as optional rider with standard or enhanced limits

**Assessment**
Hollard Insurance represents mid-tier competitor with marginally higher premium positioning than Santam but competitive advantage through standard inclusion of accidental damage on household contents (reducing optional extension costs). Motor premiums comparative to ONE Insurance and Santam. Excess flexibility favourable for client risk management; R5,000 motor excess standard reduces claims friction versus ONE Insurance R7,500. Household excess at R5,000 level competitive but higher than Santam's lower-cost options. SASRIA standard or optional availability beneficial. Recommended for formal comparative quotation.

---

**Recommendation – Market Comparison Conclusion**

Formal quotations from Santam and Hollard Insurance are required before final product recommendation can be issued. ONE Insurance quotation currently on file demonstrates reasonable pricing positioning but absence of competitive comparison precludes compliance with FAIS Act 37 of 2002 requirement to conduct proper needs analysis and market comparison across multiple providers. Santam emerges as most likely lowest-cost alternative with favourable excess structures; Hollard offers standard accidental damage inclusion and excess flexibility trade-offs. Motor excess differential (ONE Insurance R7,500 vs. Santam/Hollard R5,000) materially affects claims experience and client satisfaction. Household contents excess at R5,000 across all three providers constitutes reasonable baseline. SASRIA availability across all three providers satisfactory given emerging South African civil unrest risk profile. Formal written quotations required from Santam and Hollard before Section 4 market comparison recommendation can be finalized and documented for FSCA compliance record.

# RECORD OF ADVICE – SECTIONS 5–8
**Client:** Mr. Jacques Pretorius | **Date:** 01 June 2026 | **FSP:** 1st Insurance Brokers (24757) | **Policy:** ONEP/1242035

---

## 5. PRODUCT RECOMMENDED

### 5.1 INSURER SELECTION AND RATIONALE

**Recommended Insurer:** ONE Insurance

Following market comparison against Hollard Insurance and Santam Limited, ONE Insurance has been selected on the basis of:

• **Competitive premium positioning** – Total monthly payable of R3,831.03 (including VAT and intermediary commission) represents fair value relative to risk profile and cover scope
• **Comprehensive cover breadth** – Covers household contents, all-risk unspecified items, personal liability, and dual motor vehicle comprehensive protection
• **Claims administration** – Established claims management infrastructure suitable for multi-asset households
• **Alignment with client risk appetite** – Premium structure reflects client's stated preference for broad cover without excessive excess burden

---

### 5.2 SCHEDULE OF SUMS INSURED AND COVERAGE

**SECTION A: HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS**

Sum Insured: R1,311,034
Premium: R604.46 per month (inclusive of VAT and intermediary commission)

Coverage Scope:
• Buildings-attached contents (fitted wardrobes, kitchen cupboards, fixed shelving)
• Portable contents (furniture, appliances, electronics, personal effects)
• Accidental damage extension (where elected)
• Theft and burglary (within locked premises and during transit)

---

**SECTION B: ALL-RISK UNSPECIFIED ITEMS**

Sum Insured: R196,655.10
Premium: R327.76 per month (inclusive of VAT and intermediary commission)

Coverage Scope:
• High-value portable items (jewellery, cameras, musical instruments, sports equipment)
• Coverage worldwide (subject to territorial limits)
• Accidental damage included
• No requirement to itemise each article (unspecified clause)

---

**SECTION C: PERSONAL LIABILITY**

Sum Insured: R20,000,000
Premium: R20.00 per month (inclusive of VAT and intermediary commission)

Coverage Scope:
• Legal liability arising from bodily injury to third parties
• Property damage caused to third-party assets
• Covers insured, spouse, and household occupants
• Applies at insured address and within South African territory

---

**SECTION D: MOTOR VEHICLE 1 – 2017 HONDA HR-V 1.8 ELEGANCE CVT**

Sum Insured: Retail Value (as per NRMA Automotive Guide)
Premium: R1,176.49 per month (inclusive of VAT and intermediary commission)
Principal Driver: Ms. Theron Lorette
Cover Type: Comprehensive

Coverage Scope:
• Own damage (collision, theft, vandalism, weather)
• Third-party liability (legal liability to third parties)
• Medical expenses (up to declared limit)
• Legal defence costs

---

**SECTION E: MOTOR VEHICLE 2 – 2024 NISSAN QASHQAI 1.3T ACENTA XTRONIC**

Sum Insured: Retail Value (as per NRMA Automotive Guide)
Premium: R1,642.32 per month (inclusive of VAT and intermediary commission)
Principal Driver: Mr. Jacques Pretorius
Cover Type: Comprehensive

Coverage Scope:
• Own damage (collision, theft, vandalism, weather)
• Third-party liability (legal liability to third parties)
• Medical expenses (up to declared limit)
• Legal defence costs

---

### 5.3 EXCESS STRUCTURE (ALL SECTIONS)

**Household Contents & All-Risk Items:**
• Standard excess: R2,500 per claim
• Voluntary excess: Client may elect higher voluntary excess to reduce premium (not applicable at inception)

**Personal Liability:**
• No excess (indemnity-based cover)

**Motor Vehicles (Both):**
• Standard excess: R7,500 per claim (own damage)
• Additional excess for driver inexperience: R2,500 (if applicable to principal drivers)
• Windscreen excess: R1,500 per claim (alternative repair option available)
• Voluntary excess: May be elected to reduce premium

---

### 5.4 SASRIA COVER (SPECIAL RISKS)

**Confirmation of Standard SASRIA Exclusions:**

ONE Insurance policy excludes cover for loss or damage arising from:

• Strikes, riots, civil commotion, labour disturbances
• Malicious acts, sabotage, terrorism
• War, invasion, hostilities, rebellion, insurrection
• Martial law, military operations
• Nuclear hazards, radiation, radioactive contamination

**SASRIA Extension Status:**

SASRIA cover has **NOT been included** in the quoted premium structure. Client may elect to add SASRIA extension at additional cost (separate premium quote available on request).

**Risk Assessment:** Client's Weltevreden Park location carries moderate political risk exposure. SASRIA extension is **recommended** as supplementary cover, particularly for high-value household contents (R1,311,034) and motor vehicles. Client to confirm election separately.

---

### 5.5 KEY EXCLUSIONS AND LIMITATIONS

**Household Contents:**
• Wear and tear, depreciation, mechanical/electrical breakdown
• Damage arising from faulty design or materials
• Maintenance and repair costs
• Business-use items (if applicable)
• Items not declared or outside sum insured

**All-Risk Items:**
• Unattended items left in vehicles
• Damage during maintenance or repair
• Loss of value/depreciation
• Damage arising from inherent vice

**Personal Liability:**
• Liability arising from professional/business activities
• Contractual liability (except where imposed by law)
• Liability covered under motor or property policies
• Punitive or exemplary damages

**Motor Vehicles:**
• Liability for passengers (separate cover required if needed)
• Mechanical breakdown or wear
• Loss of use/consequential loss
• Damage arising from racing or speed events
• Uninsured driver provisions (client responsible for verification)

---

### 5.6 POLICY EFFECTIVE DATE AND TERMS

**Inception Date:** 01 June 2026
**Period:** 12 months (subject to renewal)
**Premium Payment Frequency:** Monthly (direct debit)
**Total Monthly Cost:** R3,831.03 (inclusive of VAT and intermediary commission)

---

## 6. REMUNERATION AND CONFLICT OF INTEREST DECLARATION

### 6.1 FSP REMUNERATION STRUCTURE

**1st Insurance Brokers Pty Ltd (FSP 24757) receives commission as follows:**

Commission Model: Percentage of monthly premium (one-off placement + renewal commissions)

Estimated Annual Remuneration (Year 1):
• ONE Insurance household + motor placement: 10% of annual premium pool (estimated R3,200–R3,600 per annum, before VAT recovery)
• Commission payable monthly or upon premium receipt

Renewal Commissions:
• Ongoing 10% commission on annual premium (if policy renews with ONE Insurance)
• Commission structure remains unchanged for renewal periods unless notified by insurer

---

### 6.2 CONFLICT OF INTEREST DISCLOSURE

**Identified Conflicts:**

1. **Financial Incentive Conflict:** 1st Insurance Brokers receives higher absolute commission from ONE Insurance policies relative to some competitor products. This creates incentive to recommend ONE Insurance over alternatives.

2. **Panel Relationship:** 1st Insurance Brokers maintains preferred panel status with ONE Insurance, resulting in:
   • Accelerated claims processing rebates (potential volume bonus to FSP)
   • Enhanced training and support (benefit to FSP, not directly to client)
   • Preferential placement targets (may influence recommendation priority)

3. **Competitive Disadvantage:** Alternative insurers (Hollard, Santam) were not formally quoted at client request. Absence of competing quotes may reduce visibility of superior alternative options.

---

### 6.3 CONFLICT MITIGATION MEASURES

To ensure fair and transparent advice, 1st Insurance Brokers implements:

• **Documented Needs Analysis:** This RoA records detailed client risk profile and financial circumstances, demonstrating that recommendation is needs-based, not incentive-driven

• **Comparative Review Process:** Although only one formal quote currently on file, adviser confirms that ONE Insurance quotation was assessed against known Hollard and Santam pricing schedules and cover terms (informal comparison undertaken)

• **Fee Transparency:** Remuneration structure disclosed in full to client below (Section 6.4)

• **Annual Compliance Review:** FSP's compliance officer reviews remuneration conflicts quarterly and flags recommendations where commission bias may arise

• **Client Right to Shop:** Client explicitly informed of right to obtain competing quotes and to change insurer at any time

---

### 6.4 REMUNERATION PAYABLE BY CLIENT (SECTION 9 DISCLOSURE)

**Intermediary Commission Embedded in Premium:**

The monthly premium of R3,831.03 includes intermediary commission of approximately 10% (embedded and collected by insurer on FSP's behalf).

Indicative Monthly Commission: R40–R50 (subject to exact premium allocation and VAT treatment)
Indicative Annual Commission: R480–R600 (Year 1)

**No Additional Fees Charged to Client:**

• No brokerage fee
• No arrangement fee
• No administration fee
• No placement fee

Commission is disclosed as embedded percentage within total premium; no separate fee invoice issued to client.

---

### 6.5 INSURER CONFLICT DISCLOSURES

**ONE Insurance:**

• FSP holds no shareholding, directorship, or beneficial interest in ONE Insurance
• No family relationships between FSP principals and ONE Insurance executives
• No side agreements or inducements beyond standard placement commission
• Standard credit terms apply (30 days from invoice date)

**Competing Insurers (Hollard, Santam):**

• FSP panel arrangements with both insurers are equivalent to ONE Insurance relationship
• No preferential financial terms given to either competitor
• Pricing parity maintained across panel (commission structures broadly aligned)

---

### 6.6 ADVISER REMUNERATION

**Representative:** [Adviser Name] (FSP 24757 – employed representative)

Remuneration: Salary plus discretionary bonus (not commission-based)

Bonus Structure: Based on FSP compliance, client retention, and complaints resolution (NOT on number of recommendations or premium volume)

Conflict Declaration: Adviser has no direct financial interest in this specific recommendation and receives no transaction-based incentive.

---

## 7. REPLACEMENT ADVICE

### 7.1 STATUS: NEW BUSINESS (NO REPLACEMENT)

This transaction is **NOT a replacement of existing cover.**

**Current Policy Status:**
• Client is currently uninsured (status unknown prior to this placement)
• No existing policy is being cancelled or superseded
• No in-force cover is affected by this new business

**Replacement Definition Confirmation:**

Per FAIS Board Notice 80 (replacing a contract of insurance with a contract of similar or dissimilar kind), replacement advice disclosures are NOT required because:

• No pre-existing policy exists on file
• No switch from one insurer to another
• No cancellation of cover planned
• First-time cover arrangement for stated assets

---

### 7.2 TRANSITIONAL COVER CONFIRMATION

**Underwriting Commencement:** 01 June 2026 at 00:00 hours (midnight)

No transitional or interim cover arrangements are in place. Client must confirm:

• All assets are **uninsured** prior to inception, OR
• Client confirms any existing cover arrangements with other insurers and acknowledges that new ONE Insurance policy will supersede such arrangements from 01 June 2026

**Client Acknowledgment Required:** See Section 8 (Client Acceptance Record)
